answer.evidence: The main body is a vertical sheet of falling lava (rows 2-38) with dark and bright streaks, drawn as a front-facing face. Rows 0-3 form a flat yellow strip at the top with no front-edge line or eave shadow, so it reads as the lip of the fall, not a top surface. A bright checkered pool at rows 39-47 is a horizontal surface, but it is only about 9 rows of full-width pattern with no ellipse or receding edge, and it is a small base next to the 38-row vertical face. The width is a constant 32 across all rows, so there is no silhouette that widens and narrows. The object is a flat elevation of falling lava, with no top for the main body. Kind 'organic' fits poorly, since this is a liquid or terrain effect.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a lava column with orange, red and yellow streaks and a bubbly base, and it has no flat fills (0% near-flat coverage). The pool is the main top surface, so the object reads as a front face with a top surface, not a flat elevation. The top lip is thin and ambiguous, so this reading rests mostly on the pool.
